title: The Second Aorist
subtitle: ἔλαβον, ἦλθον, εἶδον — the strong aorist.
objectives: Recognize the second aorist as a separate stem, learned individually for each verb.
Conjugate common second aorist verbs: λαμβάνω, ἔρχομαι, ὁράω.
Understand that the second aorist has thematic endings like the imperfect but means completed action.
Distinguish first aorist from second aorist by form.

sections.heading: The second aorist
sections.body:
The second aorist is the strong aorist. It does not have the sigma infix of the first aorist. Instead, it uses a different stem and thematic endings that look like the imperfect.

The second aorist must be learned verb by verb. Common second aorists:

λαμβάνω (I take) → ἔλαβον (I took)
ἔρχομαι (I come, I go) → ἦλθον (I came, I went)
ὁράω (I see) → εἶδον (I saw)
λέγω (I say) → εἶπον (I said)

The second aorist looks like the imperfect in form (augment + thematic endings), but it means completed action like the first aorist.

sections.heading: The second aorist indicative active: ἔλαβον (I took)
sections.body:
singular
  1st   ἔλαβον      I took
  2nd   ἔλαβες      you took
  3rd   ἔλαβε(ν)    he/she/it took

  plural
  1st   ἐλάβομεν    we took
  2nd   ἐλάβετε     you (plural) took
  3rd   ἔλαβον      they took

The endings are -ον, -ες, -ε(ν), -ομεν, -ετε, -ον — identical to the imperfect active endings. The stem λαβ- is the aorist stem, distinct from the present stem λαμβαν-.

sections.heading: Other common second aorists
sections.body:
ἔρχομαι (I come) → ἦλθον (I came)
  ἦλθον, ἦλθες, ἦλθε, ἤλθομεν, ἤλθετε, ἦλθον

ὁράω (I see) → εἶδον (I saw)
  εἶδον, εἶδες, εἶδε, εἴδομεν, εἴδετε, εἶδον

λέγω (I say) → εἶπον (I said)
  εἶπον, εἶπες, εἶπε, εἴπομεν, εἴπετε, εἶπον

γιγνώσκω (I know) → ἔγνων (I learned, I came to know)
  ἔγνων, ἔγνως, ἔγνω, ἔγνωμεν, ἔγνωτε, ἔγνωσαν

These must be memorized. Most Greek verbs have first aorists; a few dozen common verbs have second aorists.

sections.heading: From Xenophon
sections.body:
Anabasis I.1.1: ἦλθον οἱ στρατιῶται.
'The soldiers came.' ἦλθον is the second aorist of ἔρχομαι.

items.prompt: What is the second aorist of λαμβάνω?
What is the second aorist of ἔρχομαι?
What is the second aorist of ὁράω?
Do second aorists have the sigma infix?
Do second aorists look like the imperfect?
items.answer: Yes, in form — but they mean completed action.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 3.7 introduces the third declension consonant stems: ὁ φύλαξ (guard), ὁ γέρων (old man), ἡ ἐλπίς (hope). The third declension is more varied than the first and second, and the nominative is often disguised. The genitive reveals the stem.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can recognize and conjugate the five common second aorists listed in this lesson and can distinguish first from second aorist by form.
